title: Two stereographic charts cover the sphere
caption: Projecting from the north pole N sends P to Q = (3, 0) but cannot reach N itself; projecting from the south pole S sends P to Q′ = (1/3, 0) and cannot reach S. Together the two charts cover every point, and neither chart alone can, since a sphere is compact and a plane is not. The same picture shows ℂP¹ as the plane plus one point at infinity.
alt: A circle (the sphere seen edge-on) with north pole N and south pole S. A line from N through P on the circle meets the horizontal axis at Q; a line from S through P meets it at Q′.
description: The circle stands for the sphere, the horizontal axis for the plane.
The line from N through P = (0.6, 0.8) meets the axis at Q = (3, 0): this is the chart missing N.
The line from S through P meets the axis at Q′ = (⅓, 0): this is the chart missing S.
Every point of the sphere is covered by at least one chart, but N is never in the first.
